newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open 1.0 pct down on U.S slide.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open 1.0 pct down on U.S slide.

text.p: The Australian share market started the week one percent weaker on the back of Wall Street's 1.9 percent slide on Friday.
"The market is being quite consistent," said Andrew Sekely, head of equities at Intersuisse Ltd in Sydney.
By 10.15 a.m. (0015 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 27.3 points lower at 2,684.1.
The downturn was led by BHP which fell 15 cents to A$16.84, in line with the overall market's percentage decline after an initial 28.5 cent dip.
"The 15 cent fall today is not much when you build in the Dow's fall," Sekely said.

BHP lost 45 cents in the last half hour's trade on Friday when John O'Connor, head of the petroleum division, became the third to resign from senior ranks, citing irreconcilable differences between him and the board.
Managing director John Prescott said in a television interview on Sunday he hoped the management turmoil was over, but that the process of restoring investor confidence would be gradual.
Rio Tinto defied the trend, up 70 cents to A$21.45.
Dealers said the past few day's gains for the global miner was as much related to its London sibling's strong performance as to investors switching from BHP.

WMC lost nine cents to A$ 7.40 ahead of Wednesday's full-year report. Analysts expect the miner to show a 44 percent fall in net profit to A$217.5 million, mainly due to last year's weak metal prices.
Most blue chips lost ground, but recent winners such as Brambles and Lend Lease fell more than average. Brambles shed 75 cents to A$27.65, while Lend Lease slid 45 to A$29.60.
"It's not surprising. Lend Lease and Brambles really have been the stars of the industrial sector (in the past few months)," one dealer said.
Analysts expect Lend Lease, a property and financial services group, to report on Thursday a rise of 13 percent in pre-abnormal profit for the year to A$317.7 million.
Solidly higher gold bullion supported gold stocks, and the sector index rose 0.8 percent in early trade.
Normandy Mining rose one cent to A$1.53, while Acacia Resources gained four to A$1.47, now fully recovered from losses triggered by Thursday's half-year result.
The banking sector did better than most, falling around 0.8 percent. Commonwealth Bank eased two cents to A$16.80 while National Bank fell 20 to A$19.43.
